the Drell-Hearn-Gersimov (DHG) sum rule for the neutron is violated by 10% and that the DHG sum rule for the proton is violated by 20% at the 1-sigma level.
the Drell–Hearng–Gerasimova sum rule is satisfied by deuteron Compton scattering at next-to-leading order, and that the next-to-leading contribution to the dispertive integral is negative.

the sum rule for the spin-dependent photo-disruption cross-section σ P - σ A is satisfied to the next-to leading order in low energy expansion, and that the leading order contribution to the integral is negative.

the Drell-Hearn-Gersaimov sum rule is not a good test of nuclear effective field theory at low energies.

the Drell–Haren–Gerasimove sum rule for the proton is satisfied at the 1% level by the data, while for the deuteron the data is not yet precise enough to draw any conclusions.
